InstructionTrue when / does
EQU(a,b) NEQ(a,b)a = b / a ≠ b
GRT(a,b) GEQ(a,b)a > b / a ≥ b
LES(a,b) LEQ(a,b)a < b / a ≤ b
LIM(low,test,high)low ≤ test ≤ high (with low > high the window wraps, as in Logix)
MEQ(source,mask,compare)the bits of source selected by mask equal compare
MOV(source,dest)copies a value; CLR(dest) writes zero
ADD SUB MUL DIV MODdest = a op b, e.g. ADD(Count,1,Count)
CPT(dest,expression)evaluates an expression: CPT(Pct,(Level*100)/Cap)
COP / CPS / FLLcopy arrays, copy synchronously, fill
AND OR XOR NOTbit by bit on whole words
SCP(in,in_min,in_max,out_min,out_max,out)scales a value along a straight line

Compares are input instructions (they sit on the left and pass power) and the math instructions are outputs that act every scan the rung is true, which is why a math rung nearly always wants an ONS, a one-scan timer bit or a counter edge in front of it. The batch preset in Part IV is a compare:

GRT(Thumbwheel,0)GEQ(Large_Bottle_Count,Thumbwheel)OTE(Batch_Done);

(Step 9: the line stops itself at the dialled number of large bottles; 0 means no limit.)

There are no ANY_TO_x functions in ladder, as in Logix. MOV converts between numeric types by moving into a destination of the type you want (a REAL into a DINT truncates toward zero, a DINT into an INT wraps), and the string instructions convert between numbers and text: DTOS and STOD for integers, RTOS and STOR for REAL.

Scaling an analog input

Analog values arrive as INT counts on a channel of a 1769-IF4. By default a reservoir’s level is already 0–100 (percent), an encoder’s pulses count up and wrap, a potentiometer is 0–100: the part’s signal description (Part III) tells you the range. On a real panel the transmitter is a 4–20 mA loop and the card gives you counts, so the Reservoir and Tank parts have a Level transmitter signal setting that hands you what the card would: 0-100 % (INT), Raw counts 0-32767 or Engineering units 4000-20000 (4 mA = 4000, 20 mA = 20000). Scaling that into a number a person can read is one CPT into a REAL tag:

4–20 mA in engineering units → percent, as a REAL. The 100.0 keeps the arithmetic in floating point
CPT(Level_Pct,(Supply_Level-4000)*100.0/16000);

The pattern is always (raw − raw_min) × (eu_max − eu_min) / (raw_max − raw_min) + eu_min, and SCP does the same in one instruction: SCP(Supply_Level,4000,20000,0.0,100.0,Level_Pct). For raw counts it is CPT(Level_Pct,Supply_Level*100.0/32767). Put the result on a Digital Display with decimal places set to 1 and the console reads 34.9 %. A compare against a REAL works the same as against a DINT: LES(Level_Pct,20.0).

A device signal can also be bound straight to a tag of yours (the tag box under the signal in Properties), and a REAL tag bound that way receives the unrounded value, bypassing the card. The card route is the one you will meet in a plant, so the lessons use it.

Try it

On the bottle line, set Supply_Tank’s Level transmitter signal to Engineering units, make a REAL tag Level_Pct, add the CPT rung above to S6_Supply, and point a Digital Display at Level_Pct with two decimals. Watch it fall with every charge. Then try the raw-counts setting and change the rung to match.

In the app: colour bands on a display

A Digital Display can change its digit colour with the value it shows. Its Colour bands property is a list of value:colour pairs: 1500:yellow, 3000:red shows the digit colour below 1500, yellow from 1500, red from 3000; <100:blue shows blue below 100. The alarm limits still win over the bands, and Flash the digits while in alarm makes an alarm blink. Put Level_Pct on one with <15:red, 15:amber, 30:green and you have the operator’s whole reading of the tank in one glance, without a rung.
